*   **Time Complexity:** Feed-forward inference is fast as it avoids per-scene optimization.
The complexity is dominated by the ViT encoder-decoder and the shallow MLPs.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Depends on the number of Gaussians ($H \times W$ per view) and the storage of SH coefficients.
The use of a shallow MLP for view-dependent appearance reduces memory compared to storing full SH tables for all views.
Pose-free operation enables generalized novel view synthesis without per-scene tuning.
The training-free VIAM may not capture complex view-independent lighting variations (e.g., shadows) as effectively as learned components.
*   **When to Use:** When high-quality novel view synthesis is required from unposed images, and computational resources for per-scene optimization are limited.
*   **When Not to Use:** When ground-truth poses are available and per-scene optimization is feasible, as traditional 3DGS may achieve higher fidelity.
When real-time inference on extremely low-power hardware is required, the ViT backbone may be too heavy.
It builds on the foundation of 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) [Kerbl et al., 2023] and pose-free feed-forward methods like NAS3R [Huang et al., 2026] and DepthSplat.
